result.title: Measuring Hallucination in Large Language Models for Cyber Threat Intelligence: An Exploratory Study
result.comment: Accepted for publication in Computers and Electrical Engineering
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in cyber threat intelligence (CTI) tasks, such as summarization and question answering. However, they may produce hallucinations, false or misleading content not grounded in the source text, which can mislead analysts and corrupt downstream security decisions. This paper presents an exploratory measurement study of hallucinations in LLM-based CTI. We introduce HalluVision, a reproducible framework that generates LLM outputs, extracts domain-specific entities using a fine-tuned named entity recognition model, and evaluates factual consistency using multiple similarity metrics. Using 4,940 real-world cybersecurity articles, we measure hallucinations in outputs from two commercial LLMs and one open-weight LLM. Measurements are validated against 100 human-annotated outputs and two established faithfulness detectors. Results show that semantic similarity aligns with human judgments, whereas entity-based metrics exhibit limited agreement. Differences between models are concentrated in question answering, while entity extraction quality limits what entity-level metrics can reveal.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建 HalluVision 框架，用微调 NER 抽取领域实体并结合多种相似度指标，在 4,940 篇网络安全文章中测量两个商用与一个开源 LLM 在 CTI 摘要和问答中的幻觉，并以 100 条人工标注和两个忠实性检测器验证；发现语义相似度与人类判断更一致，实体级指标一致性有限。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「语义度量优于实体级度量」的证据可供核查 LVR 中答案是否真正依据视觉证据、以及实体/属性级 grounding 指标可靠性的借鉴线索，但对象为纯文本 CTI，无 latent 状态或视觉通路。
